theta-proof.title: Prove a Two-Sided Big-Θ Bound
theta-proof.bodyMarkdown:
Let

$$
T(n)=n^3-3n^2-n+1.
$$

To prove `T(n) = Θ(n³)`, find positive `c₁`, `c₂`, and `n₀` such that

$$
0\le c_1n^3\le T(n)\le c_2n^3
$$

for every `n ≥ n₀`.

### Upper bound

Choose `c₂ = 2`. Dropping negative terms can only increase `T(n)`:

$$
T(n)\le n^3+1\le2n^3\quad(n\ge1).
$$

### Lower bound

Choose `c₁ = 1/2` and `n₀ = 7`. For `n ≥ 7`:

$$
3n^2\le\frac{3}{7}n^3,\qquad n\le\frac{1}{49}n^3.
$$

Therefore

$$
T(n)\ge\left(1-\frac37-\frac1{49}\right)n^3=\frac{27}{49}n^3>\frac12n^3.
$$

### Combine the bounds

$$
0\le\frac12n^3\le T(n)\le2n^3\quad(n\ge7).
$$

The threshold matters because `T(n)` is negative for some small inputs. Asymptotic definitions allow a finite prefix to be ignored.
